findings.title: Duplicates monthly price logic instead of reusing monthlyPriceMinor
findings.explanation: The PR goal is that checkout and invoices compute prices the same way as the monthly price. This function rebuilds the monthly amount from `PLANS[plan].monthly[currency] * seats` and applies its own `* 100` conversion, rather than calling the existing `monthlyPriceMinor(plan, currency, seats)`. Any rule in the monthly path (seat tiers, minimums, per-currency rounding, overrides) will silently diverge for annual pricing. Derive the annual price from `monthlyPriceMinor(...)` so there is a single source of truth.

findings.title: Hardcoded `* 100` assumes every currency has 2 minor-unit decimals
findings.explanation: Currencies such as JPY (0 decimals) or KWD/BHD (3 decimals) do not use a factor of 100. If `Currency` includes or will include any of these, invoices will be wrong by 10x or 100x. Reusing `monthlyPriceMinor`, which should already own the major-to-minor conversion, avoids this. If the amounts in `PLANS` are already in minor units, this multiplication is a bug on its own.

findings.title: Floating-point arithmetic on money
findings.explanation: `monthly * 12 * 0.9 * 100` uses binary floats (0.9 is not exactly representable), so results can land just below or above a .5 boundary and `Math.round` may round the wrong way by 1 minor unit. Work in integer minor units, e.g. `Math.round(monthlyMinor * 12 * 90 / 100)`, or use integer math with an explicit rounding rule (`(monthlyMinor * 1080 + 50) / 100` with floor division). Document the rounding rule so checkout and invoices agree.

findings.title: Magic numbers for months and discount
findings.explanation: `12` and `0.9` are embedded in the expression. Extract named constants (e.g. `ANNUAL_MONTHS = 12`, `ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PERCENT = 10`) so the discount can be changed in one place and is searchable.

findings.title: No tests and no callers wired up in this diff
findings.explanation: The description says checkout and the invoice generator will compute the price the same way, but the diff only adds the function and neither consumer uses it. Add unit tests (multiple currencies including a non-2-decimal one, seat counts of 1 and many, rounding edge cases, and consistency with `monthlyPriceMinor * 12 * 0.9`), and either wire up the consumers here or confirm a follow-up exists before launch next month.

findings.title: Input validation and naming of the contract
findings.explanation: `seats` is not validated (0, negative, or non-integer values produce odd totals). If the monthly function guards this, the reuse suggested above covers it. The comment should also state that the result is the total for the full year, not a per-month price, to avoid misuse in the UI.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Add annual plan pricing

Annual billing launches next month: twelve months for the price of 10.8 (a 10% discount). Adds `annualPriceMinor` next to the monthly price so the checkout page and the invoice generator compute it the same way.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/services/pricing.ts b/src/services/pricing.ts
index 142a18d..f738804 100644
--- a/src/services/pricing.ts
+++ b/src/services/pricing.ts
@@ -16,3 +16,9 @@ export function monthlyPriceMinor(plan: Plan, currency: Currency, seats: number)
 export function planLabel(plan: Plan): string {
   return plan === 'team' ? 'Team' : 'Business'
 }
+
+// Annual billing: twelve months with a 10% discount, in minor units for the invoice.
+export function annualPriceMinor(plan: Plan, currency: Currency, seats: number): number {
+  const monthly = PLANS[plan].monthly[currency] * seats
+  return Math.round(monthly * 12 * 0.9 * 100)
+}
```
